prize_parts.citation: for credible empirical evidence on how technology and trade exposure reshape labour demand, wages and local labour-market adjustment

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed. In round 1 I preferred B001 and listed B037 as the most serious competitor if it could be judged one coherent contribution. After the exchange I think a suitably narrow B037 citation meets that condition. The discovery is that technology and trade exposure change the demand for different kinds of labour, and that these changes can be measured in local labour markets, where adjustment is slow, uneven and persistent. Autor links the technology and trade parts, and Autor, Dorn and Hanson are the identifiable authors of the import-shock evidence. This also answers the chair's question about Katz. His skill-premium work is foundational, but it sits next to ground recognised in 2023 and partly in 2024, whereas the import-shock evidence is the least overlapping part. The case rests on two things I weigh heavily: durability and design-based evidence that has been replicated and tested. The designs have been replicated in other countries, extended and criticised for more than a decade without being overturned. That is the confirmation I conceded B001 lacks on its empirical side. I do not count the number of supporters as merit, and I would reach this view even if B037 had fewer backers. The citation should claim credible evidence on adjustment, not a settled verdict on the size of welfare effects, and it should not claim to have originated the task framework.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution and scope. The task and skill-premium strand and the import-shock strand have different primary authors, and the three-name cap forces me to drop Katz, a central figure in the education-technology race. The task framework also owes much to Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane, who are not credited. The citation must therefore be narrower than the whole technology-and-inequality literature. The size and persistence of the China-shock effects, and the robustness of shift-share designs and task measures, are still debated. The topic is close to the 2023 and 2024 prizes, and a member who weighs adjacency more heavily than I do could reasonably disagree. By moving I also give up the two-name attribution of B001, which I still regard as the cleanest on the shortlist. B001's contribution is a framework with open empirical puzzles, so it remains a strong, durable and legitimate candidate on substance.

responses.point: Hassler accepted my attribution point against B037 and kept B001 as his first alternative. He said that he and I rank the two differently on confirmation, not on importance. B037 offers replicated, design-based evidence, whereas B001 is mostly a framework and synthesis with unresolved disconnect puzzles. He also moved from Katz to Dorn because of the overlap with the 2023 and 2024 prizes.
responses.response: I now accept his distinction. In round 1 I told Teorell that unresolved puzzles do not count against the pair, and I still think they show the framework's productivity. But I conceded that they weaken the claim to a settled empirical result, and that concession matters more to me once a competitor with replicated designs is on the table. I also adopt his reasoning for Dorn over Katz. A narrower trio covers the least overlapping evidence and keeps the technology strand credited through Autor. I do not treat our agreement as independent confirmation, since we co-author and are IIES colleagues.

responses.point: Enflo prefers Autor, Hanson and Katz because the pair of strands shares one object, the changing demand for labour under technology and trade. She called Dorn in place of Katz a defensible variant, and said she would move to Autor, Dorn and Hanson if the prize should honour only the trade-shock design. She also argued that the Goldin overlap is adjacent, not identical.
responses.response: I agree with her on the shared object, and that is what lets me treat B037 as one discovery. I also agree that the Goldin overlap is adjacent and should not be overstated. Where we differ is the tiebreak between Katz and Dorn. If the overlap is thematic only, the deciding factor is the attribution of the central empirical papers, and there Dorn has the stronger claim. A Katz trio would credit the framework more, but it would leave a co-author of the import-shock papers out of the part of the work that is best identified. I accept that this puts more weight on the empirical strand than she does. Her stated condition is one the committee can decide openly, and I would not oppose the Katz variant on scientific grounds.

responses.point: Krusell argued that Obstfeld and Rogoff built a widely used framework, but that part of its value is synthesis and its signature puzzles remain unresolved. He called it a stronger agenda-setting contribution than a settled discovery, and he said Kiyotaki-Moore is a more specific mechanism that the post-2008 period tested in practice.
responses.response: I partly accept this, and it is one reason I moved. The unresolved puzzles show that the framework worked as an agenda, but they do not give the citation a confirmed empirical result to rest on. I still disagree on B025. The post-2008 episode confirms the mechanism's relevance but is not direct evidence on the collateral channel, and the size of the amplification depends on calibration. That is why I keep B025 only as an alternative. I keep B001 in the same position. Both have clean two-name attribution, and I would not argue that either is scientifically weak. Our co-authorship is disclosed below.

responses.point: Friberg prefers B022 and lists B001 and B037 as alternatives. He proposed Autor, Hanson and Dorn because the China-shock strand is cleanly attributable, and he treated B037 as possibly two bundled contributions with a contested long-run interpretation. On B022 he accepted that method versus discovery is the central objection.
responses.response: His trio is the one I now adopt, and I agree that the clean attribution is its best argument. I take his bundling concern seriously, but I answer it by narrowing the citation to evidence on labour demand and adjustment under technology and trade exposure, so it does not claim the whole skill-premium history. On B022, I would say a method that changed practice can be as prize-worthy as a framework, and my reservation is not method versus discovery. It is that the credit set is wider than any three-name prize, since Bresnahan and Reiss fall outside the cap. B037 faces a similar exclusion problem, but there it is confined to one third name and not to the structure of the achievement.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will treat the technology and trade-shock strands as one discovery. If it will not, I would rather see a prize on the trade-shock evidence alone, or fall back to B001, than a composite citation.
Dorn versus Katz as the third name. My choice rests on attribution of the central import-shock papers and on overlap with recent prizes, not on a clear difference in merit.
How large and persistent the China-shock effects are, and how robust shift-share designs and task measures are.
Whether adjacency to the 2023 and 2024 prizes should lower the weight of B037 more than I allow.
How to weigh a framework with open empirical puzzles (B001) against replicated design-based evidence. I may still be underweighting B001's durability and policy reach.
I rely on my own knowledge of the literature and have not independently verified sources.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Autor, Dorn or Hanson is apparent from my supplied profile, and none to Obstfeld, Rogoff, Kiyotaki or Moore, the candidates on my alternatives. I disclose frequent co-authorship with Per Krusell (secretary) and co-authorship with John Hassler (chair), and I am an IIES colleague of both. Both commented on my round-1 position, and Hassler now supports the same Autor, Dorn and Hanson configuration, so I do not treat that overlap as independent evidence. I also have a long collaboration with Peter Klenow, a credited name on B031, which is not in my preferred configuration or alternatives. My research on growth, structural change and firm dynamics is macroeconomic and adjacent to B001 and B025, which I now list only as alternatives. These connections are disclosed, not adjudicated.
